What Are We Forecasting?

The Target Outcome Variable

  • Target Variable (\(y_t\)): Daily Estimated Avoidable Deaths (EAD) \[\text{EAD}_t = \sum_{i \in \text{Admissions}_t} \Big[ p_i(\text{delay}_i, \mathbf{z}_i) - p_i(0, \mathbf{z}_i) \Big]\]
    • \(\mathbf{z}_i\): Baseline patient case-mix vector (age, triage acuity, comorbidities).
    • \(\text{delay}_i\): Hours delayed in ED awaiting an inpatient bed.
    • \(p_i(\cdot)\): 30-day mortality risk
  • Forecasting Objective: Daily forecasts over a 10-day horizon (\(h = 1, \dots, 10\) days ahead) using near-real-time operational data.
  • Evaluation: Days 1–5 (\(\text{MSE}_{1\text{–}5\text{d}}\)) & Days 6–10 (\(\text{MSE}_{6\text{–}10\text{d}}\)).

Key Forecasting Constraints & Rules

  • Midday Forecasting Cut-off: Forecasts for days \(D+1\) to \(D+10\) can only use information available up to midday on day \(D\).
  • Strict 3-Day Reporting Lag:
    Because of verification lags, the target variable \(y\) is only known up to \(D-3\).
    • On Day \(D\), the most recent observed target value is \(y_{D-3}\).
  • Sliding Evaluation Windows: 131 sliding 10-day forecast windows evaluated over the hold-out test period (October 2025 – March 2026).

MS-ARR Formulation

\[ y_t \mid (r_t = r) = \beta_{0}^{(r)} + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \beta_{i}^{(r)} \, y_{t-i} + \sum_{m=p+1}^{M} \beta_{m}^{(r)} X_{tm} + \epsilon_t \]

where \(\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}\!\left(0, \sigma_r^2\right)\) is \(i.i.d.\) noise.

  • To model regime dynamics, we assume that the latent process \(\{r_t\}\) satisfies the Markov property:

\[ P(r_t = j \mid r_{1:t-1}) = P(r_t = j \mid r_{t-1}), \qquad j \in \mathcal{R}, \; t \ge 2. \]

  • The transition probabilities are defined as:

\[ P = \begin{pmatrix} p_{11} & \cdots & p_{1K} \\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ p_{K1} & \cdots & p_{KK} \end{pmatrix}. \]

Notation & Definitions

  • \(y_t\) is the observed number of avoidable deaths at time \(t\),
  • \(r_t\) is the unobserved (hidden) regime at time \(t\),
  • \(X_{tm}\) are the exogenous predictors.
  • \(\beta_{0}^{(r)}\) is the regime-specific intercept
  • \(\beta_{i}^{(r)}\) are the autoregressive coefficients associated with the \(i\)-th lag in regime \(r\)
  • \(\beta_{m}^{(r)}\) are the coefficients for the exogenous covariates in regime \(r\)
  • \(K\) is the total number of regimes. Set of regimes is \(\mathcal{R} = \{1, 2, \ldots, K\}\).



Parameter Estimation of MS-ARR

Model parameters are estimated using the Expectation–Maximization (EM) algorithm, which iteratively refines the parameter vector

\[ \theta = \{\beta^{(r)}, \sigma_r^2, P, \pi \}_{r \in \mathcal{R}} \]

by maximising the likelihood of the observed EAD time series \(y_{1:T} = (y_1, \ldots, y_T)\).

EM Algorithm (The Forward-Backward Algorithm - Baum-Welch)

Let \(k\) denote the iteration index. The EM algorithm proceeds as follows:

\[ \begin{aligned} &\textbf{E-step:} \\[4pt] &\quad Q(\theta \mid \theta^{(k)}) = \mathbb{E}_{\,r_{1:T} \mid y_{1:T},\, \theta^{(k)}} \left[ \log p(y_{1:T}, r_{1:T} \mid \theta) \right] \\[14pt] &\textbf{M-step:} \\[4pt] &\quad \theta^{(k+1)} = \arg\max_{\theta}\, Q(\theta \mid \theta^{(k)}) \\[14pt] &\textbf{Iterate until convergence:} \\[4pt] &\quad \theta^{(0)} \;\rightarrow\; \text{E-step} \;\rightarrow\; \text{M-step} \;\rightarrow\; \theta^{(1)} \;\rightarrow\; \cdots \;\rightarrow\; \theta^{(k+1)} \end{aligned} \]

Forecasting with MS-ARR

\(P(r_T = i \mid O_{1:T})\) denote the filtered probability of being in regime \(i\) at time \(T\). The \(h\)-step-ahead regime probabilities are obtained according to

\[ P(r_{T+h} = j \mid O_{1:T}) = \sum_{i=1}^{K} P(r_{T+h-1} = i \mid O_{1:T}) \, p_{ij}, \qquad h \ge 1. \]

Conditional on regime \(r_{T+h} = r\), the \(h\)-step-ahead forecast of the occupancy process is obtained from the regime-specific autoregressive model,

\[ \hat{y}_{T+h}^{(r)} = \beta_{0}^{(r)} + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \beta_{i}^{(r)} \, y_{T+h-i} + \sum_{m=1}^{M} \beta_{p+m}^{(r)} \, X_{T+h,m}, \]

The final point forecast at horizon \(h\) is computed as a probability-weighted average of the regime-specific forecasts,

\[ \hat{y}_{T+h} = \sum_{r=1}^{K} P(r_{T+h} = r \mid y_{1:T}) \, \hat{y}_{T+h}^{(r)}. \]

Forecasting Pipeline

from peshbeen.models import ms_arr
from peshbeen.transformations import rolling_quantile
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
ead_dff = pd.read_csv("ead_data.csv", index_col="date")
H = 5
target_var = "ead"
cat_vars = ["day", "month", "holiday"]
train_ead = ead_dff[:-H]
future_exog = ead_dff[-H:].drop(columns=target_var)
ohe_encoder = OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False,
                            handle_unknown='ignore',
                            drop='first')
transformation_function = [rolling_quantile(
                            window_size=49,
                            quantile=0.2,
                            shift=10, min_samples=49)]
ms_mod = ms_arr(n_components=2, lags=[4, 8, 10],
                target_col=target_var,
                cat_variables=cat_vars,
                categorical_encoder=ohe_encoder,
                n_iter=100,
                lag_transform=transformation_function,
                random_state=42)
ms_mod.fit(train_ead)
forecasts = ms_mod.forecast(H = H, exog=future_exog)
